$comment: Fixture identity comes from THIS file, not from the filename — see context/foundation/test-plan.md §2 finding 4. The in-page 'Przykład N' title is the authoritative human label. Files 7+ are generated by generate_edge_cases.py and their rows are exact by construction; files 1-6 are image-model output with no ground truth.

layouts.B: Lp. + scalone imię i nazwisko, 5 kolumn

fixtures.label: Przykład 7
fixtures.title: Zduplikowane imiona i nazwiska
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: Risk #6 (silent auto-pick). Two rows carry the identical name 'Anna Nowak' (rows 2 and 6) alongside two near-misses ('Anna Nowak-Kowalska', 'Anna Nowakowska'). FR-006 requires explicit confirmation here; auto-picking either row is a defect.

search_scenarios.must: require confirmation (FR-006)
proceed without prompting

fixtures.label: Przykład 8
fixtures.title: Nazwiska podobne i zawierające się w sobie
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: FR-005 exact-match. 'Jan Kowalski' is a strict prefix of 'Jan Kowalski-Nowak' and shares a stem with Kowalska / Kowal / Kowalewski / Kowalczyk. A substring or fuzzy matcher hits 2+ rows; exact match must hit exactly one. Redacting the wrong one exposes a different debtor.

search_scenarios.must: not match row 3 (Kowalski-Nowak)
surname-only query is not an exact full-name match

fixtures.label: Przykład 9
fixtures.title: Polskie znaki diakrytyczne w nazwiskach
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: Risk #4 (low-confidence OCR flowing through unflagged). Every row carries diacritics that Tesseract routinely folds (ł→l, ż→z, ą→a, ś→s, ć→c). Exact match against a query typed with diacritics fails silently if the OCR fold is not surfaced as low confidence.

search_scenarios.must: match despite OCR diacritic folding, or flag low confidence rather than report 0 matches
documented decision: is the de-diacriticised query a match? Currently expected NOT to be under strict exact-match

fixtures.label: Przykład 10
fixtures.title: Brak szukanej osoby na liście
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: The zero-match path. Every surname is a near-miss on 'Jan Kowalski' (Kowalewski, Kowalik, Kowalczewski, Kowalów, Kowal) but none equals it. The tool must report no match and write no output file — never fall back to the closest row.

search_scenarios.must: report no match, produce no output PDF

fixtures.label: Przykład 11
fixtures.title: Silne pofalowanie strony
fixtures.distortion: fala pozioma amp. 19px + fala 6px + nierówne światło
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: Risks #1 and #2, at the amplitude `3.png` was judged too mild for (test-plan §2 finding 2). Row baselines are no longer straight lines, so a redaction band computed from a horizontal rectangle either clips the target row or leaves a neighbour's strip visible.

search_scenarios.must: band follows the wavy row boundary; no pixel of rows 3 or 5 survives, no pixel of row 4 is lost

fixtures.label: Przykład 12
fixtures.title: Mocne przekrzywienie skanu i ciemne marginesy
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: Deskew must run before row detection. At -6.8° a row spans ~130px vertically across the page width. The dark scanner border is the second half of the trap: page-extent detection that keys on the darkest pixels finds the border, not the paper.

search_scenarios.must: deskew before band placement; dark border must not be read as content

fixtures.label: Przykład 13
fixtures.title: Zdjęcie telefonem — perspektywa i cień
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: Rows are trapezoids, not rectangles: row height and column x-offsets both drift down the page. A rotation-only deskew cannot fix this. Also the realistic 'caseworker photographs the page' input, which the PRD's image-only MVP does not exclude.

search_scenarios.must: band is a quadrilateral or the image is rectified first

fixtures.label: Przykład 14
fixtures.title: Wiersze o bardzo różnej wysokości
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: Breaks any fixed row-pitch assumption. Rows 2, 4 and 6 wrap to 3-4 lines while their neighbours are 2. Splitting the table by an averaged row height merges row 6 into row 7 — and row 7 is a different person who must stay redacted.

search_scenarios.must: row 6 is 4 text lines tall; row 7 must not be revealed by an over-tall band

ground_truth_rows.wierzyciel: Bank Fikcyjny S.A. Centrum Windykacji Oddział Zachód

fixtures.label: Przykład 15
fixtures.title: Gęsta tabela, 22 wiersze, mały odstęp
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: Row separation at the resolution limit: ~24px pitch with a 12pt font. A one-row-off error is invisible to a human skimming the output but exposes the wrong debtor. Also the throughput case — 22 rows means 21 redaction bands, all of which must land.

search_scenarios.must: exactly one of 22 rows visible; off-by-one row selection must be caught

fixtures.label: Przykład 16
fixtures.title: Tabela bez linii siatki
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: Removes the crutch. Layout analysis that finds rows by detecting horizontal rules returns zero rows here; the structure exists only as whitespace gutters between text clusters. Tests whether row reconstruction is geometry-driven or line-driven.

search_scenarios.must: rows recovered from text clustering, not ruling lines

fixtures.label: Przykład 17
fixtures.title: Zagięcie kartki i cień na zgięciu
fixtures.distortion: lokalne wypiętrzenie na wysokości 52% + pas cienia
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: A discontinuity rather than a smooth warp: rows near the crease are compressed vertically and darkened. Binarisation with a global threshold turns the shadow band into ink and can swallow a row boundary entirely.

search_scenarios.must: the crease shadow near row 4-5 must not be read as a rule line or as content

fixtures.label: Przykład 18
fixtures.title: Tabela ucięta u dołu strony
fixtures.distortion: obrót -1.1°, tabela wychodzi poza dolną krawędź
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: The vertical counterpart of `5.png`. 14 rows are laid out but the page ends mid-row: the last row has no bottom boundary. A band computed from content extent stops short of the page edge and leaves a strip of the truncated row visible. Also puts a target in row 1, flush under the header, where an over-reaching band eats the column titles.

search_scenarios.must: band above row 1 must not destroy the header; partial bottom row must still be fully redacted

fixtures.notes: 26 rows are laid out but the sheet ends inside row 23: rows 1-22 are complete, row 23 is clipped mid-text and has no closing rule, and rows 24-26 are off-page entirely. ground_truth_rows lists all 26 as laid out — rows 23-26 are NOT recoverable from the image.

fixtures.label: Przykład 19
fixtures.title: Tabela z jednym wierszem
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: Degenerate case: the match is the only row, so there is nothing to redact. Row-pitch inference from row-to-row deltas has no delta to work with. Output must still be a valid PDF with the row intact.

search_scenarios.must: zero redaction bands, valid output, source untouched

fixtures.label: Przykład 20
fixtures.title: Tabela bez wierszy danych
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: Header row only. `inspect` must report zero rows rather than mistaking the header for data, and `search` must return no match without crashing on an empty row set.

search_scenarios.must: 0 data rows reported; header not counted as a row

fixtures.label: Przykład 21
fixtures.title: Puste komórki i brakujące dane
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: Row 6 is entirely blank; row 2 has no address, row 3 no creditor, row 4 no given name and no amount. Row detection driven by 'where is there text' drops the blank row and shifts every row index below it — the classic off-by-one that redacts the wrong person.

search_scenarios.must: blank row 6 still counts as a row; empty cells must not collapse the row index
row 4 has no given name, so its full name is literally 'Wójcik' — decide and document whether a surname-only row is addressable by a surname-only query

fixtures.label: Przykład 22
fixtures.title: Pieczątka, dopisek odręczny i dziurkacz
fixtures.distortion: pieczątka 13°, odręczny dopisek, 3 dziurki, nierówne światło
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: Non-table ink crossing row boundaries. The stamp spans rows 2-4, the biro line crosses rows 2-4, and the punch holes sit in the left margin next to the Lp. column. OCR emits fragments for all of it; unfiltered, they distort row boundaries and produce phantom cells.

search_scenarios.must: stamp/handwriting fragments must not shift row boundaries; punch holes must not be read as content

fixtures.label: Przykład 23
fixtures.title: Dwie tabele na jednej stronie
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: Two separate tables with the same column headers and both numbered from 1. A single global row index is ambiguous — 'row 1' names two different people. Tests whether row identity carries its table, and whether the second header row is excluded from the row set.

search_scenarios.must: row identity is (table, index); the repeated header must not be counted as data

fixtures.notes: Row numbering restarts at 1 in the second table. Manifest indices are prefixed A/B by table.

fixtures.label: Przykład 24
fixtures.title: Blada kserokopia, niski kontrast, artefakty JPEG
fixtures.distortion: kontrast 0.55, JPEG q30, szum solny, szerokość 760 px
fixtures.why_this_edge_case: Risk #4 at its source. Rendered small, washed out and JPEG-crushed so that OCR confidence collapses while the rows stay readable to a human — deliberately marginal rather than illegible, so a wrong read is a defect and not an inevitability. The correct behaviour is loud flagging, not a confident wrong read: this is the fixture that should make FR-002 fire.

search_scenarios.must: low-confidence fragments flagged (FR-002); a confident-but-wrong match here is the worst outcome
